review_candidates.description: Job Description Background: UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security. In Ethiopia, the deterioration of security conditions in northern Ethiopia since September 2026 has raised renewed concerns about displacement, civilian protection, access to essential services and differentiated impacts of conflict and recovery. Building on evidence of the gendered consequences of the conflict that began in November 2020, UN Women intends to undertake a Rapid Gender Assessment in selected areas of Tigray, Amhara and Afar. The assessment will examine how gender intersects with age, disability, rurality, displacement and return status, ethnicity and poverty. Findings will inform immediate humanitarian action, early recovery, protection risk mitigation, gender-responsive resource allocation and women’s meaningful participation in recovery and peacebuilding. Organizational setting and reporting The consultant will report to the designated UN Women RGA Coordinator / commissioning country team, supported by relevant gender, humanitarian, GBV/protection and Women, Peace and Security advisers. UN Women will confirm the designated focal point for contract administration and payments. Women-led/women’s rights organizations (WROs/WLOs), organizations of persons with disabilities (OPDs) and other relevant partners will contribute to consultations and validation, with appropriate safeguarding and resourcing. Description Of Responsibilities / Scope Of Work Purpose and objectives Produce timely, actionable, geographically specific evidence on gender-differentiated needs, risks, capacities and response gaps among women, girls, men and boys, including marginalized subgroups. Assess changes in gender roles, unpaid care, livelihoods, household and community decision-making, and ownership or control of resources. Examine access to and barriers in food, WASH, shelter, education, health and sexual and reproductive health (SRH), protection, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), livelihoods, and housing, land and property (HLP). Assess participation and influence of WROs/WLOs, women peacebuilders, OPDs and excluded groups in assistance, coordination, feedback, financing and recovery decisions. Geographic and population scope Selected sites in Tigray, Amhara and Afar will be determined according to access, severity, displacement/return patterns and partner presence. Receiving communities elsewhere in Ethiopia may be considered where relevant. Compare urban/rural, IDP, returnee and host communities, and accessible/inaccessible locations. Where direct access is unsafe, use credible secondary sources and/or remote consultations, documenting gaps and limitations. Inception, coordination and ethical preparation Consult UN Women, sector specialists and appropriately supported WRO/WLO and OPD partners; refine research questions, coverage, sampling, access/security considerations, safeguarding, quality assurance and workplan. Adapt desk-review extraction matrix and respondent-specific key informant interview (KII) and focus group discussion (FGD) guides; obtain UN Women approval before use. Secondary evidence review Review humanitarian plans, cluster dashboards, displacement/return data, protection and GBV system-level trends, SRH, education, food security, livelihoods, HLP, human-rights, Women, Peace and Security, and locally produced gender and disability evidence. Record source date, location, methods, sex-, age- and disability-disaggregated data (SADDD), reliability, access restrictions, contradictions and evidence gaps in a structured matrix. Targeted primary consultations Use a rapid, qualitative-led mixed-source design: indicative 18–30 purposive KIIs across three regions and national coordination, and 6–9 small FGDs of approximately 6–8 participants each, or individual interviews when groups are unsafe. Final targets are subject to inception approval; this is not a representative prevalence survey. Do not solicit personal violence disclosures or identifiable GBV case histories; consult providers only on system-level referral patterns. Analysis, triangulation and validation Code by region, group, change over time, needs, risks, capacities, barriers and response gaps; disaggregate by sex, age, disability and displacement status where possible. Triangulate at least two independent source types where feasible; distinguish findings from interpretations and unresolved hypotheses; disclose inaccessible areas and missing perspectives. Prioritize by severity, scale, exclusion, urgency, feasibility and evidence strength, and validate findings with local women-led partners and technical stakeholders. Reporting, recommendations and uptake Prepare a concise RGA report presenting methods, regional and population coverage, thematic findings, evidence limitations and prioritized recommendations. Produce a 2–4-page action/policy-programme brief and dissemination/uptake plan; present findings and incorporate consolidated UN Women feedback. Deliverables All deliverables shall be submitted in English in editable electronic format. review_candidates.title: Maintenance Engineer
review_candidates.description: Responsible for ensuring safe, reliable and efficient operation and maintenance of mechanical equipment and systems in a Thermal Power Plant. The role focuses on maximizing equipment availability, minimizing forced outages, improving reliability, executing preventive/predictive maintenance, troubleshooting equipment failures and supporting planned shutdowns/overhauls. 1. Mechanical Maintenance Plan and execute preventive, predictive, corrective and breakdown maintenance of mechanical equipment. Ensure equipment availability, reliability and performance in line with plant operating requirements. Diagnose equipment failures, conduct root cause analysis (RCA) and implement corrective and preventive actions. Develop equipment maintenance strategies and optimize maintenance intervals based on operating history and condition monitoring. Maintain equipment history, maintenance records, spares consumption and failure analysis. 2. Boiler & Auxiliaries Depending on assigned area, manage maintenance of: Boiler pressure parts and associated systems. Pulverizers / coal mills and feeders. Primary Air, Forced Draft and Induced Draft fans. Air Preheaters (APH). Soot blowers and associated equipment. Boiler feed pumps and other boiler auxiliaries. Valves, dampers, ducts, piping and supporting mechanical systems. 3. Turbine & Generator Mechanical Systems Maintain Steam Turbine and associated mechanical auxiliaries. Support turbine inspection, overhauling, alignment and maintenance activities. Maintain condensers, heat exchangers, pumps and associated piping systems. Monitor vibration, bearing temperature, lubrication and other critical equipment parameters. Carry out troubleshooting and support performance improvement of turbine auxiliary systems. 4. Balance of Plant (BOP) Responsible for maintenance of applicable BOP systems such as: Cooling Water / Circulating Water systems. DM Water and Water Treatment mechanical equipment. Compressed Air systems. Fire Water systems. HVAC and ventilation systems. Pumps, compressors, gearboxes, valves and piping systems. Fuel Oil and associated mechanical systems. 5. Coal & Ash Handling Where applicable, manage mechanical maintenance of: Coal Handling Plant (CHP). Conveyors, crushers, feeders, stacker reclaimers and associated equipment. Ash Handling Plant (AHP). Bottom Ash and Fly Ash Handling systems. Pumps, compressors, blowers and associated material-handling equipment. 6. Reliability & Condition Monitoring Implement reliability-centered maintenance and condition-based maintenance practices. Monitor vibration, lubrication/oil analysis, temperature and equipment health parameters. Carry out RCA for repetitive and critical failures. Identify opportunities for equipment modification, reliability improvement and life extension. Track KPIs such as equipment availability, MTBF, MTTR, breakdown frequency and maintenance cost. 7. Shutdown & Overhaul Management Prepare maintenance plans for annual shutdowns, planned outages and major overhauls. Develop job scopes, resource plans, spares requirements and execution schedules. Coordinate boiler/turbine/BOP inspection and overhaul activities. Ensure shutdown jobs are completed safely, within schedule and as per quality requirements. Review post-overhaul equipment performance and close pending observations. 8. Spares & Inventory Management Identify critical, insurance and operational spares for plant mechanical equipment. Establish minimum/maximum inventory levels based on equipment criticality and consumption. Prepare technical specifications for procurement of spares and services. Conduct technical evaluation of vendors and service providers. Drive refurbishment, repair and localization initiatives wherever technically feasible. 9. Safety, Quality & Compliance Ensure compliance with plant EHS requirements, Permit-to-Work (PTW), Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) and safe maintenance procedures. Conduct Job Safety Analysis / Job Hazard Analysis before critical maintenance activities. Ensure adherence to applicable statutory requirements, OEM recommendations and plant SOPs. Participate in safety audits, incident investigations and corrective-action implementation. Ensure housekeeping and safe work practices across maintenance areas. 10. Contractor & Team Management Supervise technicians, contractors and service agencies engaged in mechanical maintenance. Ensure adequate manpower, tools and resources for scheduled and breakdown maintenance. Monitor contractor safety, quality, productivity and adherence to schedules. Develop technical capability of team members through coaching and on-the-job training. Qualification Essential: Diploma / B.E. / B.Tech in Mechanical Engineering (Full Time) from a recognized institution. Relevant certifications in vibration analysis, condition monitoring, reliability engineering or maintenance management would be advantageous. Experience 5-12 Years of Relevant experience in Mechanical O&M / Maintenance in coal-fired or lignite-based Thermal Power Plants. Hands-on exposure to one or more areas such as Boiler, Turbine, BOP, CHP, AHP, rotating equipment or mechanical utilities. Experience in large utility-scale power plants, preferably 250 MW / 500 MW / 600 MW / 660 MW / 800 MW class units, would be preferred for senior positions. Experience in supercritical or ultra-supercritical units would be an advantage where applicable. Technical Competencies Boiler / Turbine / BOP mechanical maintenance Rotating equipment maintenance Pumps, compressors, fans, blowers and gearboxes Equipment alignment and balancing Vibration and condition monitoring Preventive & predictive maintenance Breakdown analysis and troubleshooting Root Cause Analysis (RCA) Shutdown and overhaul management Maintenance planning and scheduling Spares and inventory management SAP PM / equivalent maintenance management systems Reliability improvement and equipment performance monitoring Behavioral Competencies Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving capability Safety-first mindset Ownership and accountability Ability to work effectively in plant/site environments Team and contractor management skills Cross-functional coordination Ability to respond effectively during equipment breakdowns and plant emergencies Preferred Candidate Profile Candidates should have strong hands-on experience in Thermal Power Plant Mechanical O&M, preferably with significant exposure to Boiler, Turbine, BOP, CHP/AHP or rotating equipment maintenance. Candidates with experience in major plant shutdowns, overhauls, reliability improvement, failure analysis and maintenance optimization will be preferred
